# Tilde 0.4.3
This release includes everything introduced in Tilde 0.4.2, plus:
- Fixed a first-launch error.
# Tilde 0.4.2
Wayfinder is now Tilde. This release adds a Home page for every Space, a Welcome tour that teaches the app by using it, folder-specific properties you can optionally share, and snappier day-to-day browsing.
## Home
Each Space now has its own Home page — a starting point for the work that belongs there.
- Pin folders and links for one-click access. - Pin live folder views as cards, each with its own sorting, grouping, and filters. - Widen a view when you need more room, or keep several side by side.
Click the house in the sidebar any time you want to go back.
## Learn Tilde
Welcome is a short, hands-on tour of what makes Tilde different. Lessons use a playground folder, so you can try things without touching the rest of your files.
- Command Palette, Properties, Live Groups, Spaces, Split Views, and Pinned Folders. - Short videos plus guided walkthroughs that point at the real controls. - Progress is saved, so you can pick up where you left off. - A book icon in the sidebar opens Welcome. Hide it in Appearance settings when you no longer need it.
## Folder-specific properties
Properties now belong to the folder where you create them, instead of applying everywhere by default.
- A new property stays local to that folder until you choose to share it. - **Add Existing Property** reuses a field from another folder when you do want the same one in both places. - While a property is shared, changing its name or options updates every folder that uses it. Tilde shows how many folders that is. - **Make Independent for This Folder** if one folder needs its own version. - Remove a property from a folder without deleting it from the others.
## Faster browsing
Everyday navigation does less waiting and less flashing.
- Open With menus no longer freeze before loading. - Folder lists update in place when files appear, move, or disappear.
## Fixes and polish
- **Command-F** still searches the folder you are looking at after you click into a split pane. - **New Folder with Selection** opens the folder it just created. Undo takes you back to the parent. - **Copy Path** copies the folder currently shown, not a parent further up the trail. - Nicknames now show correctly in the sidebar. - Dropping a folder onto the sidebar pins it immediately. - Drag the space dots in the sidebar to reorder Spaces. - Appearance settings now include **Hide Recents**, if you want a quieter sidebar.

This release includes everything introduced in Wayfinder 0.4.0, plus:

# Wayfinder 0.4.0
Wayfinder 0.4.0 is a substantial update focused on making everyday file work feel faster, more personal, and more dependable. It introduces local nicknames, bulk rename, a cleaner way to manage file views, richer native file actions, and clearer cloud-download feedback.
Underneath those features is a broad performance and stability overhaul. Search, folder loading, resizing, drag and drop, filesystem updates, and multi-window persistence now do less unnecessary work while preserving the state that matters: your location, selection, layout, and folder relationships.
### Nicknames: Familiar names, unchanged files
Files and folders can now have local nicknames in Wayfinder. A nickname changes how an item is presented without changing its real name on disk, so a folder such as `Internal-ID-314` can simply appear as “Client Work” inside the app.
The original name remains easy to inspect, and nicknames follow items when they are renamed or moved—even when an entire folder tree moves. Copies keep their real filesystem identity rather than inheriting Wayfinder-only metadata from the source.
Related folders are more durable too. Wayfinder now stores bookmark-backed folder identity, allowing relationships to recover when a folder is moved in Finder or by a File Provider. If a relationship cannot be resolved automatically, a new **Locate** action lets you reconnect it without rebuilding the relationship from scratch.
### Multi-file enhancements: More capable everyday file work
Multi-selection workflows have been expanded with **Rename Multiple Items** and **New Folder with Selection**. Bulk rename can replace text, add text before or after a name, or apply indexed, numbered, and dated formats. A live example shows the intended result, while validation prevents duplicate, nested, or otherwise unsafe rename plans before anything changes on disk.
### UI Changes: Polish that feels native
File views now live in a compact selector rather than occupying a second tab strip. The selector keeps switching lightweight while still letting you create, duplicate, rename, reorder, and remove views. Each view continues to preserve its own filters, sorting, grouping, columns, and widths, and Column Browser layouts can now be saved per folder.
File menus are more complete and more consistent across list and column views. Common actions—including **Open With**, **Share**, **Pin to Sidebar**, **Copy Path**, and **Reveal in Finder**—now appear in a predictable native order. Nickname editors open beside the row they belong to, and the Inspector has clearer quick actions for single and multiple selections.
Wayfinder can now ask Finder to complete supported create, copy, move, rename, and removal operations when macOS protects the destination. If a volume does not provide a Trash, Wayfinder can instead offer a clearly explained, explicitly confirmed permanent deletion.
Cloud-backed items have clearer status throughout the app. Files that are not yet local expose a direct download control, active iCloud downloads show percentage progress, and folder actions can materialize their immediate contents as one tracked operation rather than a collection of disconnected transfers.
Across the rest of the interface, popovers now resize with their content and share consistent spacing, file menus match between views, Settings commands are back in their expected native location, and the folder emoji picker has clearer sections, hover feedback, accessibility labels, and a reset action. Appearance settings cover the default file-view mode and toolbar folder titles, while focused-pane accents, full pane outlines, and the Sidebar's 8% white material overlay are now standard app styling.
Wayfinder 0.4.0 also introduces a refreshed app icon and improves process-level saving so multi-window state is coordinated reliably when the app moves into the background or quits.
### Command Palette 2.0: Faster search, browsing, and file operations
The Command Palette has been rebuilt around persistent indexed search, prepared folder snapshots, cancellable queries, and a virtualized native results list. It stays warm between uses, responds to the first character sooner, and avoids letting an outdated search continue competing with what you are typing now. Searching within the current folder uses the same index and keeps results in the existing column view instead of changing presentation modes.
### Day-to-day performance improvements
Folder updates are now much more targeted. When Wayfinder already knows which files changed, it updates those rows directly rather than refreshing the entire folder. Renames, moves, deletes, downloads, property edits, and filesystem notifications can all take this incremental path. Returning to a retained tab can also reuse its authoritative listing and replay filesystem changes instead of automatically enumerating the folder again.
Large file operations now behave as a single transaction. Multi-item drops and Shelf transfers share one plan, progress lifecycle, refresh, rollback, and undo action. Destination checks happen away from the main thread, repeated validation is reused during a drag, and a destination that appears after planning is never silently replaced.
The persistence and observation layers have been narrowed so unrelated changes no longer redraw every open surface. File-property selections use incremental indexed database updates, while Sidebar, metadata, persistence, and per-folder state notify only the parts of the app that depend on them.
Resizing has received the same treatment. Sidebar transitions and split-divider drags update the geometry that is actually visible without repeatedly rebuilding hidden tabs or unchanged file surfaces. Sidebar width is owned by the native split host, Space paging follows explicit transitions, and final layout and focus state settle once when the interaction ends.
Column Browser and Inspector scrolling now share one native horizontal gesture owner, preventing nested scrollers from competing with each other. Large drags limit expensive custom preview work, file tables avoid redundant row updates, and shared hover tracking significantly reduces repeated window-notification work.
Image operations are faster and more reliable as well. Pixel reflection and alpha processing now use Accelerate, while WebP conversion uses a threaded low-latency encoding path suited to interactive work.
### Reliability and polish
This release fixes a wide range of cases where navigation or selection could be lost, restored to a stale row, or applied to the wrong folder after a rename, move, paste, delete, undo, or filesystem refresh. Folder moves now carry Wayfinder metadata with them, including file views, pins, properties, relationships, related URLs, recents, Shelf items, tabs, and nicknames.
Cloud downloads no longer report completion before materialization has actually finished, remain stuck in a downloading state after completion, or lose progress when the same item appears in more than one view. Older background loads can no longer replace newer folder contents or cancel work owned by the current presentation.
Sidebar resizing and Space paging have been stabilized so resizing no longer changes the active Space or leaves glass and hover presentation in an incorrect state. Split panes and tabs are more resilient during rapid interaction, with fixes for blank reveals, late layout jumps, stale animation completions, unstable reordering, and tab drops.
Column Browser previews now fit inside the true horizontal scroll extent, remain above neighbouring pane chrome, and preserve vertical Inspector scrolling while forwarding horizontal gestures to the outer column track.
File-operation failures now roll back completed steps coherently, keep undo history together, and avoid refreshing once per item. Image conversion fixes cover transparency, EXIF orientation, JPEG white backgrounds, WebP alpha, cancellation, and partially written outputs. Default-folder-viewer changes are also safer: Launch Services failures leave existing bindings intact, do not overwrite a newer choice made outside Wayfinder, and provide actionable recovery guidance.

# Wayfinder 0.3.0
This release makes folders more personal and useful with folder-specific pins, properties, recent history, and related items. It also adds source-code previews and hidden-file support, alongside a substantial round of navigation, drag-and-drop, persistence, and visual improvements.
## A richer home for every folder
- Pin important files and folders inside a folder for quick access without moving or duplicating them. - Pinned items appear above the regular column contents and can be added from the file menu, by dragging, or with the Command Palette. - The folder Info panel now brings together custom properties and recent activity, and stays closed by default until you need it. - Related folders and URLs now sit alongside file-view tabs, making connected locations easier to reach without taking up a separate sidebar. - A consolidated Add menu keeps new files, new folders, file views, related folders, and related URLs in one predictable place.
## Source previews and hidden files
- The Inspector can now show fast, read-only previews with syntax highlighting for many common source-code and configuration formats. - Added preview support for Swift, JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, JSX, Python, Rust, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, Astro, shell scripts, `.env`, `.gitignore`, and more. - Code previews follow the current Light or Dark appearance and clearly explain when a file is too large, unavailable, or cannot be previewed safely. - A new Appearance setting lets you show hidden files and folders throughout file views and search.
## Better file views and properties
- File views, their layouts, custom properties, and folder-specific pins now save more consistently across tabs, panes, and app launches. - Existing setups are carried forward automatically into the new file-view system. - Files now have clearer hover states and a quick-access three-dot menu for pinning items and adding or changing their properties. - Custom properties are easier to see and edit directly from column-view rows, with clearer colored badges and compact overflow handling. - Folder titles, file-view tabs, and related items have been streamlined into a cleaner, more consistent toolbar.
## Smoother navigation and drag and drop
- Dragging over a folder can now open it automatically, making deeper drop destinations much easier to reach. - The Shelf now expands and collapses more smoothly, has clearer hover feedback, and no longer interferes with ordinary folder drags or keyboard focus. - Newly pasted or added files receive clearer arrival feedback and selection changes feel more natural. - After deleting files with the keyboard, Wayfinder keeps your place by selecting the most useful nearby item. - Sidebar spaces remain stable while resizing, without jumping between pages.
## Fixes and polish
- Improved inline renaming, including more reliable focus and filename selection for newly created items. - Fixed several cases where folder state, selection, navigation, or property changes could be lost or applied to the wrong view. - Improved tab and pane presentation, including clearer active-pane styling and more reliable switching between previously opened tabs. - Refined popovers, row actions, pinned indicators, dividers, spacing, and selection animations across the app.

# Wayfinder 0.2.0
The release adds independent tabs in every pane, recursive splits, direct manipulation across tabs and the sidebar, deeper macOS integration, and a substantial round of navigation, performance, and reliability improvements.
## A new tabbed, multi-pane workspace
- Panes can be split repeatedly to the right or downward instead of being limited to a single dual-pane layout. - Tabs can be reordered live, moved between panes, or dropped on a pane edge to create a new split. - Tabs now open and close significantly faster - Reordering tabs is much more polished than before.
## Better macOS and Finder integration
- Wayfinder can now be enabled as the default folder viewer for supported Open, Reveal, and Show requests, with controls to enable, repair, or restore the previous handler. - Folders and files opened from Finder or another app are routed into Wayfinder's existing windows and panes.
## More capable sidebar drag and drop
- Sidebar folders can be dragged directly into the main window to create a split pane. - Pinned folders can now be reordered within a group or moved between groups. - Sidebar defaults and migrations have been tightened, including removal of only the legacy seeded Projects shortcut while preserving personal folders with the same name.
## Column view, selection, and Inspector improvements
- Column widths are now saved per directory. - An optional “Right-size columns to contents” setting automatically fits columns until a manual width is chosen. - Column view should behave more 'Finder-like' with it's logic for horizontally scrolling. - A new Preview preference controls whether a single selected folder opens the preview panel; files and multi-item summaries continue to open it automatically. - Folder navigation, selection restoration, and cached column state are more consistent when moving backward, forward, or between tabs. - Empty areas in column view now expose the appropriate New File and New Folder actions. - Renaming flow now consistently works as expected.
## Safer file operations and native interaction
- Copy and move replacements now use a transactional operation path that can undo and redo both the incoming item and the displaced destination. - Failed or cancelled multi-item copy, move, trash, and restore operations roll back completed work where possible and report partial state when a rollback itself fails. - Drag-and-drop now detects existing destinations and duplicate incoming names before committing the transfer. - Inline rename, copy, paste, cloud-status controls, and embedded column controls now claim keyboard and mouse focus without changing selection unexpectedly. - File-list and column-view commands now remain attached to the pane where the interaction began.
## Settings, appearance, and smaller refinements
- Added General settings for default-folder-viewer integration and choosing how externally opened folders are routed. - Added the column auto-sizing preference and renamed workspace restoration to “Restore tabs and panes on launch” to reflect the expanded behavior. - Added an option to show or hide the current folder title beside the file-view tabs. - Added a brand-blue sidebar selection style and separate Light and Dark appearance colors for the Related sidebar. - Popovers, menus, filter/sort editors, and settings surfaces have refreshed spacing, borders, backgrounds, and presentation behavior. - The sidebar eject control, inactive tabs, pane toolbars, dividers, selection colors, and narrow-window Inspector layout received visual polish. - Double-clicking the titlebar now respects the macOS preference to minimize, zoom, or take no action. - WebP conversion now matches `cwebp`'s default encoding behavior more closely.
